chapter: California, Cats and the Fiddle, the Tatum trio
title: Cats and the Fiddle records: songs credited to the group
summary: Grimes wrote and arranged much of the group's material but never got a share; recording went easily because they rehearsed constantly, without drums.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Q. Cats and the Fiddle record dates, Songs composed by TG

Those guys had a thing of doing that I didn't know anything about. See, they were together, they started off together before I joined them. They would put everything wrote by the Cats and the Fiddle. Me, I don't know what did I know. If I was smart, if I had somebody to tell me ... but I made them all get a share, but I still never got a share. Red Buttons say, "Ain't never got a dinner." I never got a share. I wrote a lot of stuff. And I arranged all that those that was arranged. No music, just with a head, I had to come from the head.

The record dates, they were all right. Cause we know what we were doing. Wasn't nobody nervous or no nothin' cause we were workin together all that time. No problem, you know. We didn't have a drum. And I wonder now how they kept such good tempo, good time 'cause we didn't have no drum. I guess that's why I'm so tough on drummers. They don't play the drums all the way. A lot of them play like they sprained their ankle, know what I mean? ~~Bass drum~~ like the bass drum-- foot hurt or somethin'. Now and then they'll get the bass, but I mean you have to be like Jo Jones he's a drummer, man. His bass and his foot and everything, they goin' at the same time. And a few more of them. But for an example you know. A lot of guys get a foot peddle there and hardly never use it. . . .
~~We~~ We worked, and we rehearsed, you had to rehearse to remember all that stuff. Everybody had to do his part.
